paragraphs: Learning a causal graph involves identifying directed relationships among variables while ruling out directed cycles. This paper develops a polynomial-time algorithm for learning such graphs when the relationships can be nonlinear and nonparametric. It also establishes finite-sample guarantees, connecting the method’s behavior to the amount of data available rather than relying only on an unlimited-data argument.

The analysis avoids several assumptions often used to make causal discovery manageable: linear relationships, additive effects, independent noise, and faithfulness. It instead requires a condition on residual variances, the variation remaining after prediction. That condition is related to earlier equal-variance assumptions for linear models, so the result replaces familiar restrictions with a different explicit requirement.

The authors compare computational cost with an optimal algorithm that already knows the variable ordering. Relative to that informed reference, their algorithm incurs additional cost linear in the dimension and sample count. They also compare it with existing approaches in simulations. The contribution combines broader modeling flexibility with computational and statistical guarantees under the stated variance condition.
neurips-2020-a-polynomial-time-algorithm.tldr: A polynomial-time causal graph algorithm offers finite-sample guarantees for nonlinear, nonparametric models under a residual-variance condition.

paragraphs: Learned Bloom filters incorporate a machine learning classifier into a filtering system, with the aim of improving its performance. This paper focuses on information that existing learned filters leave underused: the classifier’s predicted probability scores. Treating the classifier mainly as a binary decision maker does not make full use of the distinctions present across those scores.

The proposed algorithms generalize learned Bloom filtering by using the complete range of score regions. The central idea is to let more of the classifier’s output inform the filtering procedure. This matters because the learning component supplies more information than a final yes-or-no prediction, and that additional information can affect how efficiently the filter operates.

The authors prove improvements in both false positive rate and memory usage relative to existing learned Bloom filter approaches. They also demonstrate better performance on real-world web information filtering tasks. Together, these results connect a change in how classifier scores are used to two practical objectives: reducing mistaken positive responses and reducing the storage needed for filtering.
neurips-2020-adaptive-learned-bloom-filt.tldr: Ada-BF uses the full range of classifier scores to improve learned Bloom filters’ false positive rates and memory usage.

paragraphs: A mixture model describes data through several underlying component distributions. Recovering those components becomes difficult when they overlap substantially. Earlier research established sufficient conditions under which grouped observations make a finite mixture identifiable, meaning that the components can be distinguished from the observed distribution. Those conditions can accommodate nonparametric components and even complete overlap.

This paper moves from identifiability to estimation. It proposes an algorithm that consistently estimates any identifiable mixture model from grouped observations. Consistency means that the estimates approach their targets as data accumulate. The analysis combines an oracle inequality for weighted kernel density estimation on groups with a general result linking accurate estimation of the group distribution to accurate estimation of its mixture components.

A practical version of the method handles paired observations. The reported comparisons show improvements over existing methods, particularly when components overlap strongly. The significance is that grouping can support useful component recovery even when separation in the observations is weak, provided the mixture is identifiable; the consistency claim retains that condition.
neurips-2020-consistent-estimation-of-id.tldr: The paper gives a consistent estimator for identifiable nonparametric mixtures from grouped observations, with practical gains on strongly overlapping components.

paragraphs: Active inference describes perception and action within a Bayesian framework organized around minimizing free energy. Although the theory addresses intelligence broadly, computational implementations had largely operated in simple, low-dimensional settings. This paper introduces a neural architecture that uses several Monte Carlo sampling techniques to extend active inference to complex, continuous state spaces.

The architecture selects policies through Monte Carlo tree search and trains a feed-forward habitual network to approximate that policy distribution. It also uses Monte Carlo dropout to predict future updates to beliefs about parameters and optimizes the precision of state transitions. Together, these mechanisms support learning environmental dynamics and choosing actions while maintaining task performance relative to reward-based counterparts.

In a toy environment built from dSprites, the agents develop disentangled representations suited to modeling transitions. In Animal-AI, the same architecture supports planning and reward-directed navigation even when visual input is temporarily suspended. These demonstrations suggest that sampling-based deep active inference can support both internal models of environmental change and useful behavior in more demanding environments.
neurips-2020-deep-active-inference-agent.tldr: Monte Carlo methods extend deep active inference to continuous environments, enabling learned dynamics, planning, and navigation during temporary loss of vision.

paragraphs: Models of implied volatility surfaces serve two purposes: reproducing observed market prices and valuing other financial instruments. This makes fitting the training observations important alongside predicting unseen prices. The paper develops a neural network approach to both tasks while addressing a financial consistency requirement: generated option prices should not allow portfolios that produce risk-free profits.

The proposed approach adds soft-constraint penalties to the loss and presents these as guaranteeing the absence of arbitrage opportunities. It can also work with standard volatility-surface models, supplying a neural correction when those models do not reproduce market prices accurately. This combination allows the method to be used as an addition to established quantitative finance techniques.

Empirical results indicate particular usefulness when observations are sparse or erroneous. The authors also quantify prediction uncertainty in poorly observed regions, investigate deeper versus shallower networks, and compare with standard models. Evaluating both training and test sets reflects the application’s dual objective: matching prices already seen while producing useful predictions for prices not included in fitting.
neurips-2020-deep-smoothing-of-the-impli.tldr: A neural approach fits and predicts implied volatility surfaces with arbitrage constraints and can correct classical models, especially with sparse or erroneous data.

paragraphs: Image-to-image translation becomes difficult when moving between categories requires substantial changes in shape. The authors attribute this weakness in existing methods to their high-resolution bottlenecks. DeepI2I addresses the problem through a deep hierarchy that draws on structural information in lower layers and semantic information in upper layers, bringing both kinds of features into translation.

To train these deep models on small datasets, the method transfers knowledge from pretrained GANs such as BigGAN or StyleGAN. A pretrained discriminator initializes both the translation encoder and discriminator, while a pretrained generator initializes the translation generator. Because the transferred encoder and generator do not automatically align, an adaptor network connects their representations.

Across Animal faces, Birds, and Foods, the authors report at least a 35% reduction in mFID relative to the state of the art. Their qualitative and quantitative results also show benefits from transfer learning, especially on small datasets. They additionally report the first image-to-image translations across domains containing more than 100 classes, demonstrating the approach’s use in broad category settings.
neurips-2020-deepi2i-enabling-deep-hiera.tldr: DeepI2I combines hierarchical features with pretrained GAN components to improve image translation involving large shape changes and small datasets.

paragraphs: Distributionally robust optimization studies how a model performs across a set of possible data distributions. The way that set is defined determines which changes the model is asked to withstand. This paper examines uncertainty sets built using integral probability metrics, a broad family that includes maximum mean discrepancy, total variation, and Wasserstein distances.

The central result connects distributionally robust optimization under any choice of these metrics to a family of regularization penalties. It recovers and strengthens existing results for maximum mean discrepancy and Wasserstein distances. Other choices within the same framework correspond to additional commonly used penalties, giving a unified account of how regularization relates to robustness.

The authors extend the analysis to the f-GAN objective and examine how the discriminator class shapes robustness. Their results provide theoretical support for aspects of existing penalty-based methods, including Wasserstein, MMD, and Sobolev GANs. The contribution is a set of mathematical links: choices of distributional uncertainty, training penalties, and discriminator families can be understood together when analyzing robustness.
neurips-2020-distributional-robustness-w.tldr: The paper links robustness under integral probability metrics to regularization penalties and extends that analysis to GAN objectives and discriminator choices.

paragraphs: Neural models with discrete latent variables often need to sum over many possible hidden assignments during training. For structured variables, the number of assignments can grow combinatorially. Common workarounds approximate this sum through sampling or replace discrete choices with continuous relaxations, introducing the need for specialized gradient estimators.

This paper changes how the latent distribution is represented. Differentiable sparse mappings, including sparsemax and structured variants, assign nonzero probability to a much smaller set of possibilities. The model can then sum exactly over that reduced support. Exactness applies to the resulting sparse distribution: computational savings come from representing fewer active assignments, rather than approximating their sum through sampled assignments.

The authors evaluate the strategy in a semisupervised deep generative model, a latent communication game, and a generative model with bit-vector latent variables. They report good performance across all three while retaining the practicality associated with sampling-based approximations. The results show how a sparse probability representation can make exact marginalization usable in several forms of latent-variable learning.
neurips-2020-efficient-marginalization-o.tldr: Sparse latent distributions make exact marginalization efficient by restricting the sum to assignments with nonzero probability.

paragraphs: Object categories can be organized into hierarchies, with broad categories containing more specific subcategories. Fine-grained labels provide richer information but are harder to obtain. This paper introduces Hierarchical Granularity Transfer Learning, a task that uses broad-category image annotations and semantic descriptions of hierarchical categories to recognize more specific categories.

The main obstacle is a granularity gap: the images occupy the same visual space, but the broad and specific levels have different category domains. The proposed Bi-granularity Semantic Preserving Network addresses this by constructing separate visual encoders for the different levels. A shared semantic interpreter connects them, with a subordinate entropy loss used to align their representations.

This design gives each granularity its own visual representation while using category semantics to support transfer between levels. Experiments on three benchmarks with hierarchical categories show that the network is effective for the proposed task. The findings support using broadly labeled images together with semantic descriptions to learn finer distinctions, reducing reliance on the harder-to-acquire subcategory annotations.
neurips-2020-hierarchical-granularity-tr.tldr: BigSPN transfers broad-category supervision to finer recognition by aligning granularity-specific visual encoders through shared category semantics.

paragraphs: Individual-level causal estimates can inform recommendations about which action to take for a person. In settings such as healthcare, communicating whether an estimate is trustworthy matters alongside the estimate itself. This paper integrates uncertainty estimation into a class of neural network methods for individual causal effects, making reliability an explicit part of their output.

The approach targets two situations in which recommendations can become unreliable. Lack of overlap arises when the data do not adequately support comparisons between actions for some individuals. Covariate shift occurs when the population encountered at use differs from the training population. The authors show how modeling uncertainty can help handle both situations and prevent overconfident recommendations under distribution shift.

The methodology is demonstrated with a range of leading models. Under both shift and lack of overlap, the uncertainty-equipped methods can warn decision makers when predictions should not be trusted. They also outperform standard propensity-score methods for identifying lack of overlap. The contribution is therefore a practical way to expose potential inference failure alongside individualized causal predictions.
neurips-2020-identifying-causal-effect-i.tldr: Adding uncertainty estimates to neural causal models helps flag unreliable individual recommendations under lack of overlap and population shift.

paragraphs: Vision models often lose accuracy when images are blurred or contain compression artifacts. This paper argues that standard corruption benchmarks underestimate robustness in many application settings because they omit a useful opportunity: adapting to unlabeled examples of the corruption. The argument applies when such examples are available, rather than to every deployment scenario.

The adaptation replaces batch-normalization activation statistics computed from training data with statistics computed from corrupted images. This consistently improves robustness across 25 vision models. On ImageNet-C, ResNet-50’s mean corruption error falls from 76.7% to 62.2%. For the DeepAugment+AugMix model, the reported error falls from 53.6% to 45.4%, improving the ResNet-50 state of the art described in the paper.

Even one adaptation sample improves robustness for ResNet-50 and AugMix, while 32 samples suffice to improve the stated ResNet-50 benchmark record. These findings show that access to unlabeled deployment data can materially change robustness evaluations. The authors consequently argue for reporting results with adapted statistics in corruption benchmarks and other out-of-distribution evaluations.
neurips-2020-improving-robustness-agains.tldr: Updating batch-normalization statistics with unlabeled corrupted images substantially improves measured robustness across 25 vision models.

paragraphs: Deep networks often achieve low error on both training data and held-out examples from the same population, yet explaining this behavior remains difficult. Some worst-case theories do not account for observed performance, and many proposed error bounds are numerically uninformative when evaluated. This paper asks how generalization bounds and related measures should be assessed empirically.

The authors build on an earlier large-scale study that sought possible causal relationships between generalization measures and actual generalization. They examine the evaluation methods used in that study and identify ways those methods can hide both successes and failures. This shifts attention from proposing another measure to checking whether the evaluation itself reveals what a measure explains.

The paper argues that generalization measures should be assessed through a distributional robustness framework. Its contribution is methodological: an empirical evaluation should meaningfully test the reliability of a proposed explanation. The stated conclusion recommends a different framework for conducting that evaluation, without claiming that the general problem of explaining deep-network generalization has been resolved.
neurips-2020-in-search-of-robust-measure.tldr: The paper critiques empirical evaluations of generalization measures and argues for assessing them through distributional robustness.

paragraphs: Continual learning asks a model with limited capacity to learn tasks that arrive sequentially, without knowing how many will appear. Learning a new task can interfere with earlier ones, producing catastrophic forgetting. Meta-learning offers a way to reduce that interference, but existing training procedures can be slow, require offline processing, or depend sensitively on many hyperparameters.

Look-ahead MAML, or La-MAML, is an optimization-based meta-learning algorithm designed for online continual learning. It uses a small episodic memory and incorporates adjustments to individual parameter learning rates into the meta-learning update. This gives the learning process flexibility over how strongly different parameters change as new tasks arrive.

The learning-rate mechanism connects the method to hypergradients and meta-descent, providing a basis for more flexible and efficient forgetting mitigation than conventional prior-based approaches. On real-world visual classification benchmarks, La-MAML outperforms the compared replay-based, prior-based, and meta-learning methods. The reported findings support adapting the update process itself as a practical component of learning continually from a stream of tasks.
neurips-2020-look-ahead-meta-learning-fo.tldr: La-MAML combines a small memory with meta-learned per-parameter learning rates to reduce forgetting during online continual learning.

paragraphs: Graph embedding represents nodes as points in a space so that statistical methods can analyze them. Choosing the number of dimensions is consequential: a representation may require many coordinates according to its theoretical definition, especially with spectral embedding. This paper examines whether that high dimension reflects the full geometric complexity of the embedded data.

The authors show that existing random graph models, including graphon models and other latent-position models, predict that embedded points should lie near a much lower-dimensional set. The distinction is between the dimension of the surrounding representation space and the dimension of the structure the points actually occupy. A high-dimensional embedding can therefore contain substantial lower-dimensional organization.

This result suggests a way to address the curse of dimensionality: use statistical methods that exploit the hidden manifold structure. The implication is conditional on the structure predicted by the models under study. Rather than treating every embedding coordinate as an independent source of complexity, analysis may benefit from the more compact geometry underlying the node representations.
neurips-2020-manifold-structure-in-graph.tldr: Common random graph models predict low-dimensional manifold structure inside potentially high-dimensional spectral embeddings.

paragraphs: Microcontrollers have far less memory than mobile phones, making substantial neural-network inference difficult. MCUNet tackles this constraint by designing the network architecture and inference software together. Its two components, TinyNAS and TinyEngine, coordinate model selection with execution efficiency to support ImageNet-scale inference on these small devices.

TinyNAS first adjusts its architecture search space to the resource constraints, then searches for a specialized network within that space. TinyEngine schedules memory using the overall network topology rather than optimizing each layer separately. The authors report 3.4-fold lower memory use and 1.7–3.3-fold faster inference compared with TF-Lite Micro and CMSIS-NN, allowing the system to accommodate larger models.

MCUNet achieves over 70% ImageNet top-1 accuracy on a commercial microcontroller, with 3.5-fold less SRAM and 5.7-fold less Flash than the stated quantized MobileNetV2 and ResNet-18 comparisons. Visual and audio wake-word experiments also show leading accuracy with lower memory use and faster execution. These results demonstrate the practical value of coordinating architecture search with the inference engine under tight hardware constraints.
neurips-2020-mcunet-tiny-deep-learning-o.tldr: MCUNet jointly designs neural networks and their inference engine to deliver ImageNet-scale accuracy within microcontroller memory constraints.

paragraphs: Additive models are useful for regression and variable selection when observations have many dimensions. Existing approaches often focus on one task, use mean squared error, and rely heavily on prior knowledge of relationships among variables. The paper addresses settings where that knowledge is insufficient and noise is more complex than the usual squared-error formulation handles well.

Multi-task Additive Models combine additive hypothesis spaces, a mode-induced metric, and a regularizer that accounts for structure within a bilevel optimization framework. The approach is designed to discover variable structure without requiring it in advance. It also accommodates difficult noise patterns, including skewed noise, heavy tails, and outliers, while learning across multiple tasks.

The authors provide a smooth iterative optimization algorithm with convergence guarantees. Simulations and analysis of Coronal Mass Ejections data show competitive performance for both robust estimation and automatic structure discovery. The contribution brings these objectives into one formulation, so that handling complex noise and learning relationships among variables can be addressed together rather than requiring a predefined structure.
neurips-2020-multi-task-additive-models-.tldr: Multi-task Additive Models combine robust estimation with automatic variable-structure discovery without requiring prior structural knowledge.

paragraphs: A scene contains distinct objects, but a neural network’s internal representation does not necessarily preserve that organization. This can make it harder to represent how familiar objects combine in new ways. Slot Attention is an architectural component that converts perceptual features, such as the output of a convolutional network, into a set of abstract representations called slots.

The slots are exchangeable: each can become associated with any object in the input. They specialize through several rounds of competitive attention, allowing the representations to organize around different parts of the scene. Their content is task-dependent, so the module provides a way to build object-oriented representations within a broader learning system.

The authors test Slot Attention on unsupervised object discovery and supervised property prediction. In these experiments, it extracts object-centric representations that support generalization to previously unseen compositions. The finding matters because compositional organization is built into the resulting representation: the system can represent objects as separate units whose combinations may change across scenes.
neurips-2020-object-centric-learning-wit.tldr: Slot Attention turns perceptual features into exchangeable object-centered representations that empirically support generalization to unseen compositions.

paragraphs: Visual trackers commonly use either object detection or template matching, and each approach suits different kinds of scenes. Combining them is appealing, but their different operating principles make straightforward fusion problematic. This paper introduces DTNet, an ensemble that decides online which tracking approach should take responsibility in the current scene.

Its decision mechanism uses hierarchical reinforcement learning to develop a switching strategy. Detection and template trackers compete to perform tracking where each is most capable, making selection between methods part of the tracking process. The paper also introduces a detection tracker designed to avoid the common problem of incorrect proposals.

The reported experiments show state-of-the-art tracking performance together with a good balance between accuracy and efficiency. These findings support an ensemble design in which the central learned behavior is choosing the appropriate tracker as conditions change. The contribution combines that decision mechanism with the new detection component, addressing both the coordination of different tracking approaches and a specific failure source within detection-based tracking.
neurips-2020-online-decision-based-visua.tldr: DTNet uses hierarchical reinforcement learning to switch between detection and template trackers according to the scene.

paragraphs: Weighted model integration supports probabilistic reasoning with both discrete and continuous variables, including logical and arithmetic constraints. This flexibility makes it useful for expressing complicated distributions, but exact inference can be computationally demanding. The paper studies the structural boundary between problems that permit efficient exact inference and those that require a more practical approximation.

The theoretical analysis identifies a tree-shaped structure with logarithmic diameter as necessary for exact, efficient inference in the tractability characterization. This places a substantial restriction on the problems covered by efficient exact solvers. The algorithmic contribution responds by relaxing the problem structure and carrying out exact inference on the resulting approximate model.

Unlike sampling-based approximations, the proposed solver uses iterative message passing to recover some dependencies lost during relaxation. Its answers are approximate because the model has been changed, even though inference on that model is exact. Experiments suggest competitiveness with other state-of-the-art WMI solvers, connecting the theoretical restrictions to a practical strategy for working beyond them.
neurips-2020-probabilistic-inference-wit.tldr: The paper characterizes tractable weighted model integration and proposes a sampling-free approximation based on relaxed structures and iterative message passing.

paragraphs: A three-way tensor organizes information along three dimensions, and CP decomposition expresses it through constituent factors that reveal interactions among those dimensions. Finding the unknown factors leads to a nonconvex optimization problem. The paper addresses limitations of existing guaranteed algorithms, which incur irreducible error and require all factors to follow the same structural pattern.

The proposed online factorization algorithm permits different structures across factors: one satisfies incoherence conditions, while the others are sparse. Under stated conditions on initialization, rank, and sparsity, the authors prove exact recovery at a linear convergence rate. Recovery is understood up to scaling and permutation, preserving the usual ambiguity in how equivalent factors are represented.

Synthetic and real-world evaluations report stronger performance than related techniques, complementing the recovery analysis. The importance of the result is the combination of heterogeneous factor structure and a guarantee without the irreducible bias described for earlier methods. That guarantee depends on the specified structural and initialization conditions; it is not presented as applying to arbitrary tensor factorizations.
neurips-2020-provable-online-cp-parafac-.tldr: An online tensor factorization algorithm exactly recovers mixed incoherent and sparse factors at a linear rate under stated initialization, rank, and sparsity conditions.

paragraphs: An agent may need to explore an environment before knowing which reward will define its eventual task. This paper studies that reward-free setting with linear function approximation. It aims to obtain efficient learning guarantees under assumptions closer to those used for learning from an already collected batch of data.

The analysis assumes low inherent Bellman error and that the linear representation space is sufficiently explorable. The first condition concerns how well the representation supports the value-iteration updates; the second ensures that exploration can gather the information needed within that space. Under these conditions, the authors establish strong probably approximately correct guarantees for learning a near-optimal value function.

The paper provides a computationally tractable algorithm whose exploration supports a near-optimal policy for any linear reward revealed after learning. If rewards must themselves be estimated from the exploration samples, the resulting policy retains guarantees of the same order. This connects reusable, reward-independent exploration with later task solving while keeping the representation and explorability assumptions explicit.
neurips-2020-provably-efficient-reward-a.tldr: Reward-free exploration can support near-optimal policies for later linear rewards under low Bellman error and sufficient explorability.

paragraphs: Regularization helps neural networks express useful assumptions about data, including resistance to adversarial perturbations and relationships between multiple modalities. Many regularizers describe desirable properties of hidden-layer outputs. Yet training usually adjusts network weights, so those output properties are enforced indirectly through changes to the parameters that produce them.

This paper inserts a proximal mapping as a network layer. The layer directly produces regularized hidden representations, bringing the desired constraint into the computation of the representation itself. The key architectural change is therefore where regularization acts: it becomes an explicit operation on hidden outputs within the network.

The authors establish connections between this technique, kernel warping, and dropout. They also develop algorithms for robust temporal learning and multiview modeling, reporting improvements over state-of-the-art methods in both applications. These results give concrete uses for the broader design idea: a network can incorporate an operation tailored to regularizing its internal representations, providing another way to encode assumptions about robustness or relationships across views.
neurips-2020-proximal-mapping-for-deep-r.tldr: Proximal mapping layers directly regularize hidden representations, with reported gains in robust temporal learning and multiview modeling.

paragraphs: Continuous-control algorithms depend on estimates of how valuable actions will be. DDPG can overestimate those values, which can hurt performance. TD3 reduces that problem but can introduce substantial underestimation. This paper investigates the Boltzmann softmax operator as a way to improve value estimation while addressing these opposing forms of bias.

The authors first analyze the operator in continuous action spaces. They then identify a useful property within actor-critic algorithms: softmax helps smooth the optimization landscape. This provides a second reason for using it, beyond adjusting estimation bias, by connecting the value-estimation operation to the behavior of the optimization problem.

Two algorithms apply the idea to different estimator designs. SD2 uses a single estimator, while SD3 builds on double estimators. The paper reports that these methods can improve overestimation and underestimation bias, and extensive continuous-control experiments show SD3 outperforming state-of-the-art methods. The contribution combines theoretical analysis of the operator with practical algorithms and empirical evidence for the double-estimator version.
neurips-2020-softmax-deep-double-determi.tldr: Softmax-based value estimation smooths actor-critic optimization and improves estimation bias, with SD3 showing strong continuous-control results.

paragraphs: CART regression trees repeatedly split data into two groups, selecting a variable and split point that most reduce squared-error impurity. This paper studies the statistical behavior of that familiar procedure. It asks what controls training error and how tree construction and pruning can balance model complexity against fit.

The analysis links training error to the Pearson correlation between the response and the best single-split predictor within each node. To bound that correlation, the authors construct a prior distribution over split points and solve a nonlinear optimization problem. This connection translates the quality of local splits into a tool for understanding the tree’s overall fit.

Using that relationship, the paper shows that CART with cost-complexity pruning achieves an optimal complexity-versus-fit tradeoff when depth scales logarithmically with sample size. Prediction-error convergence rates are governed by data-dependent quantities that adapt to dimensionality and hidden regression structure. The result explains how the statistical behavior of CART can reflect the structure of the particular learning problem.
neurips-2020-sparse-learning-with-cart-a.tldr: A correlation-based analysis explains CART’s training error and establishes an optimal pruning tradeoff when tree depth scales logarithmically with sample size.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning often assumes a reward function is available to guide exploration. That assumption is less suitable when one set of experience must support many skills or competing objectives. This paper defines task-agnostic reinforcement learning: an agent explores without reward guidance, then uses the collected trajectories and sampled task rewards to learn policies for multiple tasks.

The proposed UCBZero algorithm finds policies within a specified tolerance of optimality for N arbitrary tasks. Its exploration bound grows logarithmically with N, alongside dependence on the horizon, numbers of states and actions, and required accuracy. A lower bound also contains a logarithmic dependence on N, showing that this dependence cannot generally be eliminated in the sampled-reward setting.

The paper separately studies the easier case where the true reward functions are known after exploration. There, UCBZero has a sample-complexity bound independent of the number of tasks. These results clarify how reusable exploration can support many later objectives and how the cost changes depending on whether rewards are known or must be learned from samples.
neurips-2020-task-agnostic-exploration-i.tldr: UCBZero explores without rewards and supports many later tasks, with logarithmic task-count dependence that is unavoidable when rewards are sampled.
